question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Intervals on Which a Function is Invertible Given Its Graph
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/b02c2e94e144935f0ff96846cd51b5a969fa8f884a7ca1d09abb231b7c945232.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible? 

I. $x\in (-4,-2)$

II. $x\in [-2,3]$

III. $x\in [-3,3]$
question.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.  

- The given function is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in (-4,-2)$ and $x\in [-2,3].$ Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/53fe88780b2ccb7522d2f1baa711162ec99300c2a2d4da29bba9ca532026cd07.png)

- The given function is **not** invertible on  the interval $x\in [-3,3]$  because some lines will  intersect the curve at more than one point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/63cee4fc05ab17a8e69d9bfae578fa83c24d73e4677065a54a33a25e0871e718.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
